Questions.Question: How many players can a club put on its main squad list?
How many places in the main squad list are reserved for locally trained players, and how many of those can be association-trained?
Questions.Answer: According to regulation 31.04, eight places in the main squad list (List A) are reserved exclusively for 'locally trained players.' Of these eight places, no more than four can be filled by 'association-trained players.'

Questions.Question: A club registers a new player during the qualifying phase and that takes List A to 26 names. What must it do?
What is the minimum number of goalkeepers a club must register?
Questions.Answer: Each club must register at least three goalkeepers in total across List A and List B, with at least two of them included on List A.

Questions.Question: What are the age and tenure conditions for putting a young player on List B?
Questions.Answer: A player may be registered on List B if they are born on or after 1 January 2004 and have been eligible to play for the club since their 15th birthday for an uninterrupted period of two years, or a total of three consecutive years with a maximum of one loan period outside the club to a team from the same association for not longer than one year. Players aged 16 may also be registered on List B provided they have been registered with the participating club for the previous two years without interruption.

Questions.Question: Can a club add new players to its squad after the league phase ends?
How many substitutions is a team allowed during a match?
Questions.Answer: A team is allowed up to five substitutions during a match. Additionally, a sixth substitution is permitted exclusively during extra time in knockout matches. Substitutions can be made using a maximum of three stoppages in play during regular time, with one additional stoppage allowed during extra time. Substitutions made before the start of the match, during half-time, between the end of normal playing time and the start of extra time, or at half-time during extra time do not count toward the limit on stoppages in play.

Questions.Question: What happens if a knockout tie is level after both legs?
Questions.Answer: If a knockout tie is level after both legs, two 15-minute periods of extra time are played at the end of the second leg. The team that scores more goals during extra time qualifies for the next stage. If both teams score the same number of goals or no goals are scored during extra time, the winner is determined by a penalty shoot-out.

Questions.Question: What share of stadium capacity has to be made available to visiting supporters, and is there a price limit?
Questions.Answer: According to the UEFA Champions League regulations, at least 5% of the UEFA spectator capacity must be made available to visiting supporters. Additionally, the price of the tickets allocated to visiting supporters must not exceed the price paid by home supporters for tickets in a comparable sector of the stadium and cannot exceed €50 (Paragraph 45.01).

Questions.Question: How many medals do the winning and losing finalists receive?
Questions.Answer: The winning team is presented with 50 gold medals, and the runner-up is presented with 50 silver medals.

Questions.Question: If a club only has six locally trained players available, what happens to the size of its squad?
Questions.Answer: If a club only has six locally trained players available, the maximum number of players that can be registered on its List A is reduced to 23 players (25 total players minus the 2 missing locally trained player slots), as stated in Paragraph 31.08.

Questions.Question: Two clubs finish the league phase on the same number of points. How is the higher position decided?
Questions.Answer: If two clubs finish the league phase with the same number of points, their ranking is decided by applying the following criteria in order: (aa) superior goal difference in the league phase; (bb) higher number of goals scored in the league phase; (cc) higher number of away goals scored in the league phase; (dd) higher number of wins in the league phase; (ee) higher number of away wins in the league phase; (ff) higher number of points obtained collectively by their league phase opponents; (gg) superior collective goal difference of their league phase opponents; (hh) higher number of goals scored collectively by their league phase opponents; (ii) lower disciplinary points total (3 points for a red card, 1 point for a yellow card, 3 points for expulsion via two yellow cards in one match); (jj) higher club coefficient as per Annex D.

Questions.Question: A player is sent off in the last league phase match. Does that suspension carry into the knockout rounds?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a suspension resulting from a red card (sending off) in the last league phase match does carry into the knockout rounds. According to paragraph 63.01, a player sent off by the referee is automatically suspended for the next match in UEFA club competitions, which includes all stages of the competition, such as the knockout rounds.

Questions.Question: A club's first-choice goalkeeper is injured for two months. Can they bring in a replacement, and does the replacement have to be locally trained?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a club can bring in a replacement goalkeeper if their first-choice goalkeeper is injured for at least 30 days. The replacement goalkeeper does not have to be locally trained, even if the injured goalkeeper was. This is permitted under Article 31.14(aa) of the UEFA Champions League regulations, provided that the club submits the necessary medical evidence and completes the official registration of List A with UEFA.

Questions.Question: How long must an outfield player be out before he can be replaced, and is that the same threshold as for a goalkeeper?
Questions.Answer: An outfield player must be out for at least 60 days due to long-term injury or illness before they can be replaced. A goalkeeper, on the other hand, has a threshold of 30 days of long-term injury or illness to be considered for replacement. These thresholds are different for outfield players and goalkeepers.

Questions.Question: Two clubs turn up with clashing shirts. Who has to change — and is the answer different in the final?
Questions.Answer: During all competition matches other than the final, the home team generally has to change its colours if the referee notices a colour clash, as stated in paragraph 40.02. However, for the final, if there is a colour clash, the team designated as the away team must wear alternative colours, as per paragraph 40.03.

Questions.Question: Can two clubs owned by the same investment group both play in this competition?
Questions.Answer: No, two clubs owned by the same investment group cannot both play in the UEFA Champions League. According to paragraph [5.01], a club cannot have direct or indirect involvement in the management, administration, or sporting performance of another club participating in a UEFA club competition. Additionally, paragraph [5.01](cc) specifies that no individual or legal entity may have control or influence over more than one club in the competition, where control includes holding majority voting rights or having decisive influence over the club's decisions.

Questions.Question: A match is abandoned at half-time and resumed the following day. Which players can take the field?
Does a player's passport determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement?
Questions.Answer: No, a player's passport does not determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement. Instead, this is based on a player's training history with the club ('club-trained player') or with clubs affiliated to the same association ('association-trained player'), as described in paragraphs 31.06 and 31.07.

Questions.Question: A player left off both squad lists picks up a ban. Can he sit it out while unregistered?
Questions.Answer: No, a player cannot serve a suspension while being unregistered. Only players who are duly registered with UEFA on List A or List B can validly serve pending suspensions, as per paragraph 31.02.

Questions.Question: After a defeat, is the head coach personally required to speak to broadcasters, and how quickly must the press conference start?
Questions.Answer: Yes, after a defeat, the head coach is personally required to speak to broadcasters during post-match interviews as per paragraph [80.01(ee)]. Additionally, the head coach must attend the post-match press conference, which must start no later than 20 minutes after the final whistle, as per paragraph [80.02].

Questions.Question: Can a club choose which ball is used for its home fixtures?
Questions.Answer: No, a club cannot choose which ball is used for its home fixtures in the UEFA Champions League. Regulations specify that for the qualifying phase, the match balls must comply with the IFAB Laws of the Game and the UEFA Equipment Regulations (paragraph 50.01). For matches from the play-offs onwards, the official UEFA Champions League match ball determined by the UEFA administration must be used (paragraph 50.02).

Questions.Question: Does Liverpool's registered squad satisfy the locally trained player requirement?
Questions.Answer: Liverpool's registered squad does satisfy the locally trained player requirement. According to Article 31.04, a minimum of eight places on List A must be reserved exclusively for locally trained players. Liverpool's squad has three club-trained players and two association-trained players, totaling five locally trained players. Since Liverpool has registered a total of 20 players on List A, this is permissible under Article 31.08, which allows for a reduction in the maximum squad size when fewer than eight locally trained players are included.

Questions.Question: Manchester United are short on club-trained players. How many can they actually register on List A as things stand?
Questions.Answer: Manchester United currently have 3 club-trained players. Regulation 31.04 mandates that 8 places on List A must be reserved for locally trained players, including a maximum of 4 association-trained players. Since Manchester United have only 3 club-trained players, they are 5 short of the required number of 8 locally trained players. As per regulation 31.08, for each missing locally trained player, the total number of players they can register on List A is reduced accordingly. Thus, Manchester United can register a maximum of 20 players (25 - 5 = 20) on their List A as things stand.

Questions.Question: Real Madrid have registered the goalkeepers shown in their squad. Are they compliant on that front?
Questions.Answer: Real Madrid are compliant with the UEFA Champions League regulations for the registration of goalkeepers. They have registered two goalkeepers on their List A (Thibaut Courtois and Andriy Lunin), meeting the requirement stated in paragraph 31.13, which mandates having at least two goalkeepers on List A and at least three in total (List A and List B combined).
